purpose: Adversarially test linear syndrome compression, hashing, and affine-span reachability on the exact v1.8 zero-syndrome formulation.

unsat_proof: (x1 OR x2) and (x1 OR NOT x2) force x1=1.
Then (NOT x1 OR x3) forces x3=1.
Then (NOT x3 OR x4) and (NOT x3 OR NOT x4) force x4=1 and x4=0 simultaneously.

soft_occurrence_model.definition: Give every literal occurrence its own Boolean variable-side bit, keep all clause constraints and negative-literal complement semantics, but drop equality between different occurrences of the same original variable.
soft_occurrence_model.syndrome_coordinates: For variable occurrence lists [0,2,4], [1,3], [5,6,8], [7,9], use consecutive XORs, giving six GF(2) consistency coordinates.
soft_occurrence_model.verified_syndrome_set: Exactly GF(2)^6 minus the zero vector: all 63 nonzero syndromes occur, and zero does not.

theorem.name: NO_DIMENSION_REDUCING_LINEAR_ZERO_HASH_IS_SOUND_ON_V1_9_WITNESS
theorem.statement: Let H:GF(2)^6 -> GF(2)^r be linear with r<6. If a soft factor is accepted whenever H(syndrome)=0, then H accepts at least one soft factor of the frozen UNSAT formula.
proof: Since r<6, H is noninjective and ker(H) contains a nonzero vector s.
The verified soft syndrome set contains every nonzero vector of GF(2)^6, hence contains s.
That soft factor has H(s)=0 although the original formula is UNSAT. Therefore the compressed zero test has a false positive.
theorem.affine_span_corollary: The soft syndrome set contains every standard basis vector and therefore has full linear/affine span GF(2)^6. Any decision rule that replaces exact zero membership by membership in the linear or affine span is also unsound on this witness.

killed: Any deterministic linear syndrome compression to fewer than the six witness coordinates followed only by a zero test
Random linear hashing used as a one-sided exact zero-membership oracle without additional nonlinear verification
Affine-span or linear-span reachability as a substitute for exact feasible-syndrome membership
not_killed: Nonlinear polynomial-size representations of the feasible syndrome set
Augmentation algorithms that preserve exact combinatorial feasibility rather than only syndrome span
A bespoke algorithm exploiting the disjoint variable-block and subcubic structure

next_target.name: E8_EXACT_FEASIBLE_SYNDROME_AUGMENTATION_V2_0
next_target.directive: Stop compressing syndromes linearly. Characterize the exact feasible-syndrome set under basic factor augmentations and seek a polynomial zero-membership algorithm that preserves nonlinear compatibility. Test every proposed closure/augmentation rule against the frozen full-nonzero witness before promotion.
